suggestions: Review the product contract in the diagnostic. For NLB path rules, use an ALB or move HTTP routing behind the NLB; recheck TLS requirements.
Use the reported required_instances as a CPU-only lower bound. Compare more instances with larger hosts, then rerun memory and database connection checks.
Compare a larger primary with reducing write CPU cost. Read replicas do not increase primary write capacity.
Compare smaller per-instance connection pools with connection pooling. Recheck demand after changing service instance counts; raising the database limit alone is not evidence of capacity.
Compare larger-memory hosts with reducing per-request memory; additional instances cannot fix a request that exceeds one instance.
Supply the missing capacity or workload inputs identified by the trace before drawing conclusions.
Check both sides of the affected connection and the TLS termination and upstream protocol settings.
Review the overloaded resource budget and downstream dependencies. Increase declared capacity only when supported by measurements or provisioning changes.
Compare traffic shaping with a revised rate policy, and verify downstream capacity before increasing the limit.
